The soil sample was teeming with *microbes*.

gloss: A small brewery that makes beer in limited quantities.
examples: A new *microbrewery* opened by the train station.
There are six *microbreweries* within ten miles.
The *microbrewery* only sells out of its own taproom.

gloss: A small thing that has the same features as something much larger.
examples: The school is a *microcosm* of the whole city.
That one street is a *microcosm* of the housing crisis.
Small towns can be perfect *microcosms* of national politics.

gloss: A flat sheet of film holding many pages of a document in miniature.
examples: Back issues are only available on *microfiche*.
The librarian showed me how to load the *microfiche*.
He spent all afternoon reading *microfiche*.
contrast: The ending is said like *feesh*, from French *fiche*.

gloss: Film holding greatly reduced photographs of documents or pages.
examples: The census records are stored on *microfilm*.
She scrolled through *microfilm* looking for the obituary.
The archive is slowly moving off *microfilm*.

gloss: A unit of weight equal to one millionth of a gram.
examples: The dose is measured in *micrograms*.
One *microgram* is a thousandth of a milligram.
The label lists 400 *micrograms* of folic acid.
contrast: A *microgram* is a thousand times smaller than a *milligram* — an easy mix-up on labels.

gloss: The use of microscopes to examine very small things.
examples: The lab specializes in electron *microscopy*.
*Microscopy* confirmed what the blood test suggested.
The course includes a week of hands-on *microscopy*.

gloss: One millionth of a second.
examples: The switch responds in a few *microseconds*.
He hesitated for a *microsecond* and then said yes.
The delay is under two hundred *microseconds*.

gloss: Surgery on very small structures, done with a microscope and tiny instruments.
examples: The hand was reattached with *microsurgery*.
*Microsurgery* can take eight hours or more.
She trained in *microsurgery* in Boston.

gloss: A point up in the air, off the ground.
examples: The dog caught the frisbee in *midair*.
Two planes nearly collided in *midair*.
He stopped the sentence in *midair* and started over.

gloss: The part of something that is equally far from each end or side.
examples: There's a stain right in the *middle* of the rug.
He woke up in the *middle* of the night.
The *middles* of these cookies are still soft.

gloss: A boxer or wrestler in the weight class between welterweight and light heavyweight.
examples: He fought as a *middleweight* for six years.
Two *middleweights* are on the undercard.
She's the new *middleweight* champion.

gloss: The central area of a soccer or football field, or the players who work there.
examples: They lost control of *midfield* after halftime.
The pass was intercepted at *midfield*.
Our *midfield* is the strongest part of the team.
